question.text: Ms. Ananya Desai is onboarding investors for Ganga Infra Trust (a Category II AIF launched exclusively for non-accredited investors). Which of the following statements about subscription thresholds is CORRECT under SEBI (AIF) Regulations?

answer.text: Minimum investor ticket is INR 1 crore and minimum scheme corpus is INR 20 crore (except Social Impact Funds where minimum corpus is INR 5 crore)
Minimum investor ticket is INR 25 lakh and minimum scheme corpus is INR 50 crore
Minimum investor ticket is INR 2 crore and minimum scheme corpus is INR 100 crore
Minimum investor ticket is INR 50 lakh and minimum scheme corpus is INR 25 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: As per Regulation 10(c) and the investor subscription rules under the AIF Regulations, the minimum investment per investor in an AIF is INR 1 crore (not applicable to Accredited Investors). Each scheme must have a minimum corpus of INR 20 crore, reduced to INR 5 crore for Social Impact Funds. Employees/directors of the AIF or Manager may invest a minimum of INR 25 lakh. The Trap: Option B swaps employee minimum (INR 25 lakh) with general investor minimum. Option C inflates figures toward Special Situation Fund thresholds (SSF min corpus INR 100 cr, investor INR 10 cr). Option D fabricates values. The AI framework relaxes the INR 1 cr minimum for Accredited Investors only. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A Distributors test the same thresholds from the sale-side. XXI-A PMS Distributors have their own minimum (INR 50 lakh PMS investment) — different product, different floor. XIX-E Cat III follows the same INR 1 cr / INR 20 cr structure, so the numbers are AIF-wide except Social Impact Fund carve-out. Manager's Pro-Tip: Raising from 20 LPs at INR 1 cr each gives you corpus of INR 20 cr — the bare floor. Most Cat II PE funds target 50-70 LPs to avoid concentration (single-LP > 50% triggers specific DD under SFA standards for QIB/QB/ICDR evergreening checks).
